actions: Launched a new Sculptra campaign on Nov 9 with three ad sets and three image ads. Meta approved two of the ads and did not approve the third.
Raised the wellness event campaign budget from $26.60 to $40 a day on Nov 9.
Added a new version of the wellness event ad with a surprise gift for early bookings, in its own ad set, on Nov 6.
Added a new ad set for the 'Your wellness questions deserve real answers' event ad on Nov 9 and updated that ad.
Switched off one event test ad set on Nov 6 and turned the pellet specialist ad set back on Nov 9.
Updated the returning-visitor audiences on Nov 9 to leave out people who already filled in the event form.

campaigns.campaign_name: KS/MM- DCT- Wellness Event- La Bella Sea Girt- Lead- CBO

insights.creative: The ad that opens 'Hormone pellet specialists do not usually sit in a treatment room for five hours answering questions' brought 5 of the 6 Meta leads at $16.77 each. It sells the event as one afternoon of real answers, with same-day bloodwork, a gift card raffle and a free consult for early bookings. The 'Your wellness questions deserve real answers' ad brought 1 on $67.83. Worth testing a second ad built on the specialist's time and access, since that angle beat the perks-first ads this week.
insights.doing: 5 leads reached the CRM this week at $44.27 each, down from 9 at $18.61 the week before, on $221.33 of spend. Meta counted 6.
insights.look_into: Cost per CRM lead more than doubled while spend went up. The new event ad with a surprise gift for early bookings spent $43.78 with no leads, and one of the new Sculptra ads was not approved by Meta.
insights.next: We recommend moving more of the event budget to the ad that opens on the pellet specialist, since it brought 5 of the 6 Meta leads at $16.77 each, and checking how many event leads have booked a time slot.
